chk_problem.reason: High aggregate accuracy in neural morphological generation systems can conceal systematic errors clustered in rare morphological subclasses.

chk_method.reason: Orthography-aware diagnosis and causal isolation using controlled ablation experiments.

chk_data.reason: Japanese verb inflection dataset in morphological transduction format, converted to hiragana, with 3,958 verbs.

chk_setup.reason: A mentions an 80/10/10 train/development/test split, while B mentions eight ablation conditions.

chk_primary_result.reason: Type 4-2 verbs, comprising <1% of data, account for 30–43% of residual errors and contribute 34–48× their prevalence to total errors.

chk_secondary_result.reason: Removing Type 4-2 verbs alone improves accuracy more than removing all irregular verbs combined.

chk_baseline.reason: A describes the baseline as the full-data performance of the PGT and LST models, while B provides specific accuracy numbers for the baseline.

chk_conclusion.reason: A attributes error concentration to the interaction between low-frequency patterns and orthographic processes, while B emphasizes the need for fine-grained evaluation.

chk_limitation.reason: A mentions ablation experiments run only once per condition and a correlational analysis, while B emphasizes the focus on two architectures and the need for cross-linguistic validation.
